agent.name: Silver-Milk Team Organizational Adoption Agent
agent.specialty: Organizational readiness for an emerging-technology application at the stage asked (preparation, bounded evaluation, routine operation): eight dimensions rated from case facts with owners, failed vs. absent vs. unknown kept apart, execution gates kept separate from readiness gaps, one verdict by table with a stage ladder, actions traced to gaps, and specific requests for missing evidence (adoption decisions are handed to the Adoption Agent)

analytical_question: Assuming strategic appropriateness, can this organization staff, govern and sustain a bounded internal concept-board evaluation, and what organizational changes and evidence are required before separate authorization?
general_et_finding:
EVIDENCE BASE: Supplied cards
UNIT: Text-to-image diffusion models; latent diffusion reference architecture.
DEMAND [D1]: Moderate — adapt sponsorship to probabilistic visual generation.
DEMAND [D2]: High — add generation-specific prompting and output-evaluation skills.
DEMAND [D3]: High — add explicit synthetic-output screening and rejection provisions.
DEMAND [D4]: Moderate — adapt computing access, input handling and storage provisions.
DEMAND [D5]: Moderate — adapt resource allocation to generation and review costs.
DEMAND [D6]: High — add provisions for synthetic-content risks, provenance and input rights.
DEMAND [D7]: Moderate — adapt change handling to generated visual content.
DEMAND [D8]: Moderate — adapt operational accountability to generation and review.
TECHNOLOGY LIMIT: Reliable factual fidelity is not guaranteed by plausible visual output. This is a conservative inference from the supplied generative-AI risk context, dated July 2024, rather than a current benchmark of latent diffusion. The supplied cards contain no architecture-specific fidelity measurement.
application_finding:
FIT: Partial — flexible visual generation supports exploratory concept boards, but exact product-detail fidelity requires separate judgment.
TASK SIDE: Variable creative briefs combine aesthetic exploration, reference-image interpretation and review; frequency is unspecified, interdependence includes final-material handoff, and criticality rises if concepts imply inaccurate product attributes.
TECHNOLOGY SIDE: Text-conditioned generation offers visual variation and iterative interaction; usability, integration, reference handling and security depend on the implementation and terms, while generated plausibility does not establish accuracy.
FIT GAP: Faithful preservation of specific product details.
APPLICATION ADDS: D3 — distinguish exploratory imagery from approved factual product representation through an explicit review boundary.
UPSTREAM READ: case-premise — Assignment 6 conditionally favored preparing a bounded internal comparison, not immediate execution or rollout; no formal DEFER GATE or POSTURE GATE was supplied.
organization_specific_finding:
PREMISE: Adoption is assumed strategically appropriate; adoption decisions belong to the Adoption Agent.
UNIT OF ANALYSIS: Two-person marketing operation, dependent on the store owner's authorization and tool-rights review by a role yet to be identified.
STAGE ASKED: Bounded evaluation — trial execution is the earliest stage requiring new authorization and resources beyond preparation.
D1 Leadership/sponsorship: Not ready — the owner has not explicitly sponsored an AI trial; no AI evaluation sponsor is designated — Owner: none stated.
D2 Skills/training: Insufficient evidence — visual-editing experience exists; AI-specific training and competence are unconfirmed — Owner: none stated.
D3 Workflow/process: Insufficient evidence — manual boards and designer fallback exist; AI review checklist and repeatable acceptance measures are unconfirmed — Owner: none stated.
D4 Infrastructure/data: Insufficient evidence — catalogue references exist; an approved evaluation environment and permitted inputs are unspecified — Owner: none stated.
D5 Resources/budget: Insufficient evidence — staff-hour allocation, availability and approved budget are unknown — Owner: none stated.
D6 Governance/risk: Not ready — no AI evaluation sponsor or accountable pilot lead is designated, and no alternative role is stated with authority to clear tool/input permissions — Owner: none stated.
D7 Culture/change: Insufficient evidence — staff attitudes, objections and change feedback are unknown — Owner: none stated.
D8 Operating ownership: Not ready — neither an accountable pilot lead nor ongoing operating owner has been designated — Owner: none stated.
STRENGTHS: Two employees already edit visual content; catalogue references are available; manual boards and a freelance designer remain available.
GAPS THAT COULD CAUSE FAILURE: D1 absent AI sponsorship; D6 absent assigned evaluation approval authority; D8 absent accountable evaluation leadership.
EXECUTION GATES: Tool selection and applicable vendor/input-use permissions — clearing owner unassigned, to be assigned by the store owner; separate trial authorization — store owner, inferred from existing concept approval, with AI authority requiring explicit confirmation. Open terms themselves do not lower ratings.
OPERATING OWNER: None currently exists.
COUNTS: Ready 0, Partially ready 0, Not ready 3, Insufficient evidence 5
READINESS VERDICT: Not ready — D1, D6 and D8 are required dimensions.
VERDICT BASIS: Both — observed blockers determine the verdict; missing evidence limits the remaining assessment.
VERDICT SENSITIVITY: All unknowns Ready: Not ready; all unknowns Not ready: Not ready.
STAGE LADDER: PREPARATION: Supported — no stated prohibition on commissioning planning. BOUNDED EVALUATION: Blocked — D1, D6 and D8 lack designated accountable roles. ROUTINE OPERATION: Blocked — no ongoing operating owner exists; all eight dimensions would be required.
FAILURE LOCUS: Organization

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: COMPETING READING: Undetermined — more evidence — existing owner approval and marketing capability might extend to a small evaluation if their authority and responsibilities were confirmed.

STRONGEST CASE AGAINST: Not ready could be too pessimistic if current concept approval already includes explicit AI evaluation sponsorship and accountable coordination. However, the case expressly says these designations have not occurred. It could understate difficulty if protected capacity or input permissions subsequently prove unavailable.

DISTINGUISHING EVIDENCE: A dated owner-approved responsibility record, obtained by 2026-12-22, identifying the AI sponsor, evaluation lead, permission-clearing authority and their accepted responsibilities would settle whether the explicit ownership blockers have changed.
Contrary observations: Existing visual-editing skills, catalogue references and retained manual/designer fallback provide useful starting capabilities, but do not demonstrate AI evaluation readiness.

Evidence gaps: No field interviews, trial traces, current tool-rights inspection, staffing commitments or measured benefits are supplied. NIST was inspected this run only as context; the other inherited external sources were not rechecked.
confidence_and_uncertainty: VERDICT CONFIDENCE: High — the case explicitly states required sponsorship and ownership are undesignated, so unknown dimensions cannot reverse the present verdict. Confidence would change if dated responsibility assignments superseded those premises. Confidence about any real retailer is low: this is a hypothetical case without fieldwork, and class-level fit has no current task-specific benchmark.
value_opportunity_implication: A separately authorized evaluation could examine whether concept variety or creative usefulness justifies generation, correction and review effort against the manual/designer workflow. These are proposed opportunities; no savings, quality improvement or business value has been observed. Preparation can make the staffing and review burden visible before authorization.
risk_governance_implication: Preparation does not authorize uploading catalogue assets or running a tool on real inputs. AI-specific authorization, permission-clearing responsibility and stop authority remain unassigned; existing concept approval does not establish them. Human product-detail review, permitted-input boundaries, internal-only handling, escalation and manual fallback need application-specific evidence. Manual/designer fallback is supplied, but its AI-specific escalation procedure is not demonstrated. Internal use reduces publication exposure without resolving confidentiality, fidelity or workload risks. No safety or legal certification follows.
recommendation_management_implication:
READINESS VERDICT: Not ready (Bounded evaluation) — required sponsorship, approval accountability and evaluation ownership are absent.
MOST CONSEQUENTIAL GAP: D8 Operating ownership — without an accountable lead, staffing and product-detail review cannot be coordinated responsibly.
MOST CONSEQUENTIAL MISSING FACTOR: D5 Resources/budget. QUESTION: What protected employee and reviewer hours, budget and backfill can the owner approve without impairing ongoing marketing?
ACTION 1 [D1]: Explicitly designate an AI evaluation sponsor and decision/stop authority — GAP: owner has not sponsored an AI trial — OWNER: store owner (stated) — DONE WHEN: a dated responsibility record names the sponsor and accepted authority, separately from trial authorization.
ACTION 2 [D8]: Assign an accountable evaluation coordinator and review accountability — GAP: no accountable pilot lead is designated — OWNER: store owner (stated) — DONE WHEN: named role holders accept coordination and fidelity-review duties in writing.
ACTION 3 [D6]: Assign responsibility and authority for tool/input-permission clearance and escalation — GAP: no AI-specific approval role is designated — OWNER: store owner (stated) — DONE WHEN: a dated responsibility record identifies who can clear permissions, escalate concerns and stop use.
NOW: Map the manual workflow, interview staff about capacity, document proposed review duties and assemble a permission/authorization checklist without using the tool on real inputs.
change_monitoring_triggers: TRIGGER [D1]: By 2026-12-22, a single signed responsibility charter establishes accepted sponsorship, governance clearance authority and evaluation leadership, closing D1/D6/D8 → Undetermined — more evidence, with D3/D4/D5 still unresolved.
The present Not ready verdict has no lower category. Additional adverse evidence would change the blocker set, not the verdict.
REVIEW DATE: 2026-12-22 — six weeks from the 2026-11-10 assessment.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: MORE INFO → D5 Resources/budget: Request owner-approved employee/reviewer hours, budget, backfill and workload commitments — WHY IT MATTERS: capacity may remain a required-stage blocker after ownership is assigned.

MORE INFO → D3 Workflow/process: Request the AI-specific fidelity-review checklist, acceptance measures, reviewer responsibilities, escalation/fallback procedure and any demonstration record — WHY IT MATTERS: existing manual fallback does not establish the evaluation review process.

MORE INFO → D4 Infrastructure/data: Request the proposed environment, approved evaluation scope, access/storage arrangements and permitted catalogue inputs — WHY IT MATTERS: establishes whether required evaluation infrastructure and input handling are available.

MORE INFO → D2 Skills/training: Request this tool's skills evidence and the role accountable for any training — WHY IT MATTERS: determines a nonrequired bounded-evaluation dimension and a required routine-operation dimension.

INTAKE MISSING: 2 — AI sponsor and decision/stop authority explicitly absent; 3 — evaluation coordinator and permanent operating owner explicitly undesignated; 4 — approved environment/scope and input permissions unknown; 5 — current-tool contract/control coverage unknown; 6 — budget, protected hours and backfill unknown; 7 — application-specific review, fallback, escalation and demonstration evidence unknown; 8 — governance review roles and scope unknown; 9 — tool-specific skills evidence and training ownership unknown; 10 — objections, feedback channels and unsanctioned use unknown. Stage and intended internal-use scope are supplied.
